source.title: NLS ground states on metric trees: existence results and open questions

accepted.question_text: For the nonlinear Schrödinger energy E(u,G) = (1/2)∫_G |u′|² dx − (1/p)∫_G |u|^p dx on the rooted binary metric tree T_o or the unrooted binary metric tree T, with exponent p in (2,4), mass μ > 0, mass-constrained space H^1_μ(G) = {u in H^1(G): ∫_G |u|² dx = μ}, ground-state energy L_G(μ) = inf_{u in H^1_μ(G)} E(u,G), best Poincaré constant λ_1, and threshold μ_G^* = max{μ ≥ 0: L_G(μ) = (1/2)λ_1 μ}, is μ_G^* strictly positive?
accepted.context_brief: Positivity of the non-radial threshold mass for p in (2,4)

evidence.quote: Given a metric graph G, a number p ∈ (2,6) and a mass μ > 0, the ‘ground state problem’ on G is the minimization problem min_{u∈H^1_μ(G)} E(u,G), where E(u,G) is as in (1) and H^1_μ(G) is the class of mass-constrained functions H^1_μ(G) := {u ∈ H^1(G) : ∫_G |u|^2 dx = μ}.
Assume G = T (or G = T_o) and p ∈ (2,6), and define μ_G^* := max { μ ≥ 0 : L_G(μ) = 1/2 λ_1 μ }.

Remark 1.3. When p ∈ (2,4) we are not able to prove that μ_G^* > 0: if, as we believe, this was the case, then at μ = μ_G^* a transition would occur from nonexistence to existence of ground states (exactly as when p ∈ [4,6)), while, if μ_G^* = 0, then ground states would exist for every mass.

accepted.question_text: For the nonlinear Schrödinger ground-state minimization problem on the rooted binary metric tree T_o or unrooted binary metric tree T at the exponent p = 4, with threshold μ_G^* = max{μ ≥ 0: L_G(μ) = (1/2)λ_1 μ}, do ground states of mass μ = μ_G^* exist?
accepted.context_brief: Existence at the non-radial threshold mass for p = 4

evidence.quote: Assume G = T (or G = T_o) and p ∈ (2,6), and define μ_G^* := max { μ ≥ 0 : L_G(μ) = 1/2 λ_1 μ }.
Finally, when p = 4, we do not know whether ground states exist or not, with a mass μ = μ_G^*.

accepted.question_text: For the nonlinear Schrödinger ground states on the rooted binary metric tree T_o or unrooted binary metric tree T, is every ground state necessarily radial, meaning that its value at any point depends only on the geodesic distance |x| from the chosen root vertex o?

evidence.quote: A function u ∈ H^1(T_o) is called radial if its value at any point x ∈ T_o depends only on |x|, the geodesic distance of x from the root o of the tree (the same definition applies to functions u ∈ H^1(T), choosing as o an arbitrary vertex of T).

Unfortunately, the usual techniques of radial symmetrization are not effective in this setting, and it remains an open problem to establish whether ground states (on T_o or on T) are necessarily radial functions.
Since, however, the radiality of ground states is an open issue, the two problems should be considered as distinct, until proven otherwise.

accepted.question_text: For the nonlinear Schrödinger energy on the rooted binary metric tree T_o or unrooted binary metric tree T, does the unrestricted ground-state energy level L_G(μ) equal the radially restricted ground-state energy level L_{G,r}(μ) for the same mass μ, where L_{G,r}(μ) = inf_{u in H^1_{μ,r}(G)} E(u,G) and H^1_{μ,r}(G) consists of the mass-constrained radial functions?
accepted.context_brief: Equality between free and radial ground-state energy levels

evidence.quote: H^1_{μ,r}(G) := { u ∈ H^1_μ(G) : u is radial } where G = T_o or G = T, and study the minimization problem min_{u∈H^1_{μ,r}(G)} E(u,G), i.e. the ground state problem restricted to radial functions.
L_{G,r}(μ) := inf_{u∈H^1_{μ,r}(G)} E(u,G), μ ≥ 0, and we will call radial ground state (of mass μ) any function u ∈ H^1_{μ,r}(G) that achieves the infimum in (14).

In the light of this, the problem raised in Remark 1.3 would be solved, if one could prove that ground states are in fact radial functions or, at least, that L_G(μ) = L_{G,r}(μ) (note that the inequality ≤ is trivially satisfied).

Title from page 1. Section hierarchy: Abstract (p1); 1 Introduction (pp1-7, including Notation on p7); 2 Inequalities and a priori estimates (pp7-11); 3 Existence and non-existence of ground states (pp11-15); 4 Radial ground states: proof of Theorem 1.4 (pp15-19); References (pp19-21). Likely open-question regions are Introduction pp3-5 and radial proof comment p16.
Remark 1.3 explicitly states the authors cannot prove μ_G^*>0 for p in (2,4).
Remark 1.3 explicitly states the authors do not know whether ground states exist at μ=μ_G^* when p=4.
The Introduction explicitly labels radiality of ground states as an open problem/open issue; page 16 notes that quadratic averaging cannot solve the symmetry question.

The Introduction states that proving L_G(μ)=L_{G,r}(μ) would solve the issue raised in Remark 1.3, presenting equality of free and radial levels as an unresolved route independent of proving radiality of all ground states.
Expanded the raw statement using the source definitions of E, H^1_μ(G), L_G(μ), λ_1, and μ_G^* from pages 3-4.
Expanded the threshold-existence question using the definition of μ_G^* from page 4.
Expanded radiality using the source definition of radial functions from page 4.
Expanded equality of levels using the source definition of the radial constrained problem and L_{G,r} from page 5.
Kept four candidates: q_001 and q_002 are distinct threshold-regime questions; q_003 concerns symmetry of minimizers; q_004 concerns equality of free and radial energy levels.
